title: Dr. Strange
edition: 1978 US television pilot directed by Philip DeGuere, with Peter Hooten and Jessica Walter
synopsis: A hospital psychiatrist cares for Clea Lake after Morgan le Fay takes control of her. Lindmer asks him to enter the astral realm to bring her back.
verdictRationale: Strange follows up on a patient whose distress others can quiet with sedation. His concern for Clea is admirable, and Morgan’s use of her body against another person is frightening. The proposed Neutral verdict also weighs the film’s presentation of astral travel and initiation into sorcery as desirable ways to heal.
ageRationale: Clea loses control of her actions, pushes someone over a railing and later sees Morgan in mirrors. The fear that a person cannot trust her own movements may linger after the dated effects.
reflection: Clea first needs someone to take her fear seriously. Families can consider how to sit with a frightened patient even when no one yet understands what is wrong.

themes.name: Compassion and service
themes.evidence: Strange seeks Lindmer’s help and goes after Clea when she slips into a coma. Her safety motivates his entry into the astral realm.

themes.name: Coercion
themes.evidence: Morgan commandeers Clea’s body and makes her push Lindmer. The violation initiates the conflict and follows Clea into the hospital.

themes.name: Occult or misleading spirituality
themes.evidence: Lindmer guides Strange in astral travel. Learning to exercise this power is central to the pilot’s heroic succession story.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: The plot and viewer guide do not cover every encounter. Screen the Hooten pilot and record explicit dialogue and visual evidence.

title: Doctor Strange: The Sorcerer Supreme
edition: 2007 Lionsgate animated DVD feature, 76 minutes, Jay Oliva; Bryce Johnson voices Strange
synopsis: Strange walks away from a mother whose daughter lies in a coma. An injury to his own hands sends the surgeon in search of a new teacher, and the children’s nightmares acquire a face he recognizes.
verdictRationale: Gina challenges a gifted doctor who has withdrawn from other people’s suffering. The memory of his sister April gives his withdrawal a human cost. His return to help the children is worth discussing, while the film makes mastery of occult power the answer to their peril.
ageRationale: A child briefly wakes from a coma in terror, a parent begs for help, and magical combat reduces bodies to skeletons. These images can disturb a viewer even in animation.
reflection: There is a difference between being unable to cure someone and abandoning the person who asked for help. April’s death helps explain why Camille’s mother finds Strange so hard to reach.

themes.name: Compassion and service
themes.evidence: Gina challenges Strange over the children and he eventually opposes the power behind their suffering. His response to the ward marks his change.

themes.name: Pride
themes.evidence: When Camille’s mother begs for help, Strange leaves. Gina’s rebuke names the cost of his self-absorption in a pivotal early scene.

themes.name: Occult or misleading spirituality
themes.evidence: Training in sorcery and the battle against Dormammu supply the central route to protection. The film presents the mantle of sorcerer as an honor.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: A content-guide entry on sex does not address every reference to family or identity. Screen the 76-minute animated feature.

title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
edition: Sam Raimi’s 2022 theatrical MCU feature, 126 minutes, Benedict Cumberbatch and Xochitl Gomez
synopsis: Wanda pursues America Chavez, whose power could reunite Wanda with children in another universe. Strange must decide whether protecting America requires taking control of her gift.
verdictRationale: Wanda’s grief is recognizable, but the terror of the children she wants to mother exposes the harm of trying to possess them. Strange finally trusts America to act. Alongside that change, the film gives its hero a victory assisted by forbidden magic and the use of a corpse. Those choices complicate the spiritual assessment.
ageRationale: A man’s head implodes, another character is cut in two, and an animated corpse figures prominently in the finale. These horror images are more sustained and bodily than a typical superhero chase.
reflection: America allows Wanda to see the children’s fear from the other side of her wish. Love has to make room for the child who actually stands before the adult, including the child who says no.
